text.arabic_uthmani: أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْا۟ أَنَّا جَعَلْنَا حَرَمًا ءَامِنًۭا وَيُتَخَطَّفُ ٱلنَّاسُ مِنْ حَوْلِهِمْ ۚ أَفَبِٱلْبَٰطِلِ يُؤْمِنُونَ وَبِنِعْمَةِ ٱللَّهِ يَكْفُرُونَ

words.gloss_range: compound interrogative connector opening a resumed rebuke
words.prose: {{ar:أَوَ}} ({{tr:ʾa-wa}}) begins with both question and connection alive. The ayah does not open as a detached inquiry; it resumes the prior warning (29:66) and launches a rhetorical challenge whose answer is already implied, setting up the later inferential question as the second interrogative pillar.

topics.headline: compound question resumes prior warning
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the opening is a connected rebuke, not a neutral question.
topics.reason: The hamza plus connector is locally licensed as a rhetorical-question opening tied to the preceding discourse.

topics.headline: first pillar of a two-question argument
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the ayah framed by two interrogative turns: proof first, accusation second.
topics.reason: The later inferential question confirms that this opening belongs to a paired rhetorical structure.

words.gloss_range: jussive negator making the perception question a past-negative proof demand
words.prose: {{ar:لَمْ}} ({{tr:lam}}) pulls the following perception verb into past-negative jussive force: have they not seen. In this rhetorical frame, the negation does not weaken the claim; it makes the sanctuary proof something already available and therefore blameworthy to miss.

topics.headline: past-negative jussive makes evidence already available
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the rebuke as about evidence already seen, not a future or generic failure.
topics.reason: The particle governs the following imperfect and produces the past-negative perception frame.

topics.headline: negation covers the whole perception content
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that what they failed to recognize is the whole divine sanctuary-making clause.
topics.reason: The following content clause is syntactically governed by the perception verb under the negation.

words.gloss_range: jussive Form I perception meaning recognize observable evidence
words.root_gloss_range: root spans seeing, perceiving, judging, and forming an assessment; the local content clause selects cognitive recognition rather than bare eyesight
words.prose: {{ar:يَرَوْا۟}} ({{tr:yaraw}}) is the apocopated jussive perception verb under the negator, with the plural subject carried inside the ending. Its root range lets the question mean more than looking: they should recognize the divine agency in the following divine sanctuary-making clause. The formulaic opening also echoes observation challenges such as 29:19, now applied to sanctuary security.

topics.headline: apocopated form shows grammatical control by negation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that the opening rebuke is built into the verb form, not only inferred from tone.
topics.reason: The jussive deletion and defective verb shape match the governing negator.

topics.headline: seeing means responsible recognition of evidence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the accused group is responsible to infer from visible social reality.
topics.reason: The Form I perception verb governs the factual content clause and assigns recognition to the observers.

topics.headline: observation challenge returns as sanctuary sign
topics.reader_payoff: The reader recognizes the secure sanctuary as another sign to be read, like other observation formulas (29:19).
topics.reason: Formula rows with concrete references survive as a local observation-pattern payoff.

words.gloss_range: subordinator plus divine pronoun introducing the content of perception
words.prose: {{ar:أَنَّا}} ({{tr:ʾannā}}) turns what follows into the fact they should perceive and places divine agency before the main verb even arrives. Its {{tr:-nā}} then resonates with the {{tr:-nā}} of the following making verb, making the proof clause feel tightly marked by divine first-person agency. That embedded fact becomes the premise for the later accusation.

topics.headline: content clause makes divine agency the perceived fact
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the rebuke asks for recognition of a specific divine act, not vague awareness.
topics.reason: The subordinator introduces the content complement governed by the perception verb.

topics.headline: repeated first-person marker reinforces agency
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears divine agency reinforced before and inside the making verb.
topics.reason: The adjacent pronoun repetition is local, visible, and supports the agency focus.

topics.headline: embedded evidence prepares the later accusation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the sanctuary-making clause as the premise that makes the final accusation irrational.
topics.reason: The content clause is structurally embedded in the proof question before the accusation question begins.

words.gloss_range: perfect divine making/rendering with double-object resultative force
words.root_gloss_range: root range includes making, rendering, placing, designating, and configuring; the local double-object frame selects resultative institution rather than creation from nothing or fabrication
words.prose: {{ar:جَعَلْنَا}} ({{tr:jaʿalnā}}) is a completed divine act that takes both the sanctuary noun and the security attribute. The verb therefore does not merely say that a sanctuary exists; it presents a protected order rendered secure, a settled premise against which ongoing snatching, misplaced belief, and denial are judged. The construction also joins the sanctuary-security proof pattern seen at 28:57.

topics.headline: perfect first-person verb sets completed divine premise
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that secure sanctuary status is a completed divine act before the ongoing human failures appear.
topics.reason: The verb form and suffix license divine subject and perfect-as-settled-premise readings.

topics.headline: double object makes security part of the result
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees security as part of what was made, not an afterthought beside the sanctuary.
topics.reason: The local complements support resultative double-object force.

topics.headline: root range narrows to instituting protected order
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the sanctuary as a configured protective order, while broader fabrication or creation branches are not selected locally.
topics.reason: The local double-object construction selects rendering or instituting rather than ex nihilo creation or fabricated invention.

topics.headline: making sanctuary recurs as a proof pattern
topics.reader_payoff: The reader recognizes the making clause as part of a recurring sanctuary-security argument (28:57).
topics.reason: Concrete inter-ayah rows are coherent and support a formulaic proof relation.

words.gloss_range: accusative indefinite sanctuary as protected precinct and first object
words.root_gloss_range: root range links prohibition, sacral inviolability, protected precincts, and forbidden boundaries; the local noun selects the protected-space branch
words.prose: {{ar:حَرَمًا}} ({{tr:ḥaraman}}) is the first object of the making verb, with the following security attribute supplying its secure result. Its indefinite form lets the argument foreground sanctuary as a type of inviolable protected precinct, while the local scene points to the known protected center. That center is immediately set against people being snatched from around them, so the word carries the spatial core of the proof. The exact sanctuary-security compound is shared with 28:57, and the rare indefinite concrete form gives the category itself weight.

topics.headline: first object names the sanctuary type
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the sanctuary is the acted-upon object and a protected category, not merely a named place.
topics.reason: Accusative case and indefinite tanwin support first-object and type-designation force.

topics.headline: prohibition root produces protected precinct semantics
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees security as arising from inviolable boundary status, not generic safety.
topics.reason: The local noun and root branch license sanctuary as prohibited protected space.

topics.headline: secure center contrasts with surrounding snatching
topics.reader_payoff: The reader maps the ayah spatially: protected center inside, dangerous periphery around it.
topics.reason: The immediate circumstantial clause supplies the contrastive outside zone.

topics.headline: security compound and rare form add proof weight
topics.reader_payoff: The reader recognizes the phrase as a marked sanctuary-security proof, including the shared compound at 28:57.
topics.reason: The exact compound and rarity rows are coherent local payoffs.

words.gloss_range: active participle of security agreeing with sanctuary and completing the result state
words.root_gloss_range: root range connects safety, trust, security, and belief; this occurrence selects real secure-state meaning while preparing the later belief irony
words.prose: {{ar:ءَامِنًۭا}} ({{tr:āminan}}) locks security onto the sanctuary noun by agreement and by its role as second object or circumstantial attribute. As an active participle, it presents safety as a standing state of the sanctuary. The same root later returns in the belief verb, so real security in the proof clause becomes the foil for trust misdirected toward falsehood. Its matching {{tr:-an}} cadence helps seal the sanctuary-security phrase, a compound also attested at 28:57.

topics.headline: agreement makes security the sanctuary result
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that security is grammatically bound to the sanctuary, whether read as result or attribute.
topics.reason: The adjective or second-object analysis preserves the same local security relation.

topics.headline: participle presents enduring safety
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels security as a stable condition rather than a passing event.
topics.reason: The active participle and matching indefiniteness support an enduring attribute of the sanctuary type.

topics.headline: security root returns as misplaced belief
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the irony: real security appears first, then the same root-family is turned toward false trust.
topics.reason: The two local occurrences of the same root make the semantic reversal available.

topics.headline: stable safety faces ongoing passive snatching
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the first proof as security inside versus predation outside.
topics.reason: The following snatching clause is the immediate contrast to the secure participle.

topics.headline: security compound is formulaic and audibly paired
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the sanctuary-security phrase as a sealed proof unit, also shared with 28:57.
topics.reason: The exact collocation and paired tanwin cadence add local proof texture.

words.gloss_range: circumstantial connector introducing simultaneous contrast
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) here is best read as circumstantial: while people are being snatched. A simple coordination remains grammatically possible, but the stronger payoff is simultaneity; the secure sanctuary is visible precisely while surrounding danger continues. This first {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) contrasts with the later coordinating {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) that pairs the accusations.

topics.headline: circumstantial reading dominates but coordination remains possible
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices simultaneity: the protected state and surrounding danger coexist in the proof.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence favors a circumstantial clause while allowing a weaker coordination reading.

topics.headline: same connector shifts function later
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the ayah move from scene contrast to moral coordination through two uses of the same particle.
topics.reason: The two particles have distinct local clause functions.

words.gloss_range: imperfect passive Form V snatching as ongoing violent extraction
words.root_gloss_range: root range centers on sudden seizure, snatching, and violent extraction; the local Form V passive intensifies repeated exposure while suppressing the agent
words.prose: {{ar:يُتَخَطَّفُ}} ({{tr:yutakhaṭṭafu}}) shifts from completed divine making to ongoing passive vulnerability. The agents of seizure are not named; the people are foregrounded as patients, and the Form V passive makes the surrounding danger feel repeated or multi-directional. Its rare violent-extraction root is the harsh outer foil to the secure sanctuary, a proof pattern also linked with 28:57. The doubled middle consonant and rough guttural-emphatic-labial path make the sound pressure match the sudden seizure.

topics.headline: imperfect passive foregrounds exposed victims
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that outside danger is ongoing and patient-focused rather than a single named raid.
topics.reason: The imperfect passive deagentivizes the scene and contrasts with the completed active divine act.

topics.headline: derived passive intensifies repeated snatching
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the danger as repeated seizure from the surrounding field, not a one-off incident.
topics.reason: The Form V passive row is locally coherent with the surrounding complement.

topics.headline: rare root gives violent extraction image
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the outside world as unstable because people are violently taken out of place.
topics.reason: The root image and rarity both support marked violent-seizure force.

topics.headline: snatching clause is the contrastive second panel
topics.reader_payoff: The reader maps the proof as secure center against surrounding seizure.
topics.reason: The clause follows the secure sanctuary phrase and takes the surrounding phrase as its spatial complement.

topics.headline: rough sound texture supports seizure meaning
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the move from smooth safety to harsh seizure in the word shape.
topics.reason: The phonetic rows are local surface payoffs and do not control the parse.

words.gloss_range: definite human collective as passive subject of surrounding danger
words.root_gloss_range: root range links human sociability and familiarity, with a supplied dispute involving forgetfulness; the local noun selects the human collective under vulnerability
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلنَّاسُ}} ({{tr:al-nāsu}}) is the definite collective made passive subject of the snatching. The grammar presents people as exposed patients rather than agents, and the definite collective makes the danger recognizable as a public human condition around the addressees. The human-root associations with sociability and awareness sharpen the irony: familiar human society is prey while the protected group fails to read the lesson. The same human collective also recalls the faith-testing scene of 29:2, now placed between real security and misplaced trust.

topics.headline: definite collective undergoes snatching
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the danger is a recognizable human vulnerability, not an anecdote about unnamed individuals.
topics.reason: The passive subject relation and definite collective form are syntactically forced.

topics.headline: human-root associations color the vulnerability scene
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the irony of sociable humans appearing as prey, while the local noun remains a collective human subject.
topics.reason: Root-dispute material can color the scene but does not replace the local human collective sense.

topics.headline: human collective links danger and faith-test contexts
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees human vulnerability placed between real security and misplaced trust, with same-surah pressure from 29:2.
topics.reason: The recurrence and co-occurrence rows add a coherent contextual payoff.

words.gloss_range: spatial source preposition governing the surrounding zone
words.prose: {{ar:مِنْ}} ({{tr:min}}) makes the danger spatially precise: people are snatched from around them. Its source and separation values draw the boundary between protected center and exposed periphery, before the ayah’s later object-marking bi phrases shift the argument from geography to the moral objects of belief and denial.

topics.headline: source phrase marks removal from the surrounding zone
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees danger beginning in the space around the protected group, not as an abstract condition.
topics.reason: The preposition governs the surrounding noun as spatial complement of the passive verb.

topics.headline: prepositions move argument from space to moral objects
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that small prepositions carry the ayah from geography to accusation.
topics.reason: The spatial source preposition precedes the two object-marking bi phrases in the closing charges.

words.gloss_range: possessed surrounding zone where security gives way to vulnerability
words.root_gloss_range: root range includes aroundness, change, capacity, power, and cycles; the local noun selects spatial surrounding while allowing limited pressure from change and failed capacity
words.prose: {{ar:حَوْلِهِمْ}} ({{tr:ḥawlihim}}) is governed by the source preposition, so the surroundings become the source-zone of snatching. The suffix makes that periphery theirs: danger is around the same group being rebuked, not far away. The broader root field of change and capacity is narrowed by the local spatial use, but it still helps the periphery feel like the border where security turns into exposure.

topics.headline: governed noun marks source-zone of danger
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the threat located in their own surrounding zone, not in a distant report.
topics.reason: The preposition governs the noun and the suffix attaches the zone to the rebuked group.

topics.headline: root field colors the periphery as failed capacity
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the edge where security changes into vulnerability, while the local meaning remains spatial surrounding.
topics.reason: Broader power and change senses are relevant as coloring but are narrowed by the governed spatial phrase.

topics.headline: suffix keeps the same accused group in view
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the proof concerns the immediate environment of the same group addressed across the boundary.
topics.reason: The possessive suffix is licensed as referring to the same group in the ayah frame.

words.gloss_range: inferential interrogative hinge from proof to accusation
words.prose: {{ar:أَفَ}} ({{tr:ʾa-fa}}) is the hinge from visible proof to moral indictment. The fāʾ is resultative: given the secure sanctuary and surrounding danger, how can the next clause foreground belief in falsehood? It mirrors the first interrogative opening but now draws the accusatory conclusion.

topics.headline: resultative question draws conclusion from proof
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the second question as the consequence of the sanctuary evidence, not a new topic.
topics.reason: The compound particle opens the second rhetorical question with inferential force.

topics.headline: two rhetorical questions build proof then charge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the ayah’s logic: observed protection first, irrational object-choice second.
topics.reason: The particle marks the pivot from the first proof scene to the paired accusation.

topics.headline: second question opens paired object contrast
topics.reader_payoff: The reader anticipates the closing binary: falsehood receives belief while blessing receives denial.
topics.reason: The following fronted bi-phrases confirm the antithetical structure.

words.gloss_range: object-marking preposition attaching belief to falsehood
words.prose: {{ar:بِ}} ({{tr:bi}}) binds falsehood to the belief verb, so the charge centers on the object that receives trust. Because the prepositional phrase is fronted, falsehood is heard before the belief verb, and it balances the later blessing phrase.

topics.headline: preposition supplies the trusted object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the indictment is about where trust is placed.
topics.reason: The preposition is the required complement marker with the belief verb.

topics.headline: fronting foregrounds falsehood before the verb
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears falsehood as the focused object before the action of belief is named.
topics.reason: The proclitic and fronted phrase produce object-focus pressure.

topics.headline: matched bi phrases balance opposite objects
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the two closing objects as deliberate alternatives: falsehood trusted, blessing denied.
topics.reason: The same preposition heads both fronted object phrases in the antithesis.

words.gloss_range: definite falsehood as void object of misplaced trust
words.root_gloss_range: root range includes nullity, futility, falsehood, perishing, and voiding; the local substantive selects the evaluative category of falsehood or the void
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْبَٰطِلِ}} ({{tr:al-bāṭili}}) is the fronted genitive object of trust, definite as a known category rather than an indefinite error. Its participial shape lets falsehood feel like the voiding or collapsing thing, which makes belief in it self-incriminating. The usual falsehood-versus-truth contrast is locally recast: here falsehood stands opposite God’s blessing, the divine blessing they deny. It also resumes the falsehood-belief-denial pattern from 29:52, now adapted to the sanctuary-blessing argument.

topics.headline: definite object is foregrounded before belief verb
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the trusted object condemned before the verb names the misplaced trust.
topics.reason: The bi-governed noun remains dependent on the verb while fronted for focus.

topics.headline: lexical voidness makes trust paradoxical
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that they trust what is characterized by nullity and collapse.
topics.reason: The root and participial substantive support falsehood as an evaluative void category.

topics.headline: falsehood contrasts locally with divine blessing
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the ayah replace the usual truth-opposite with a blessing-opposite: falsehood versus God’s favor.
topics.reason: The paired bi-phrases make the local opposite the divine blessing, even though truth is the common broader contrast.

topics.headline: falsehood reprises the earlier faith-denial triad
topics.reader_payoff: The reader recognizes the charge as adapting the earlier falsehood-belief-denial pattern from 29:52.
topics.reason: Concrete same-surah recurrence supports the local triad without overriding the current object pair.

words.gloss_range: Form IV belief verb assigning trust to the void
words.root_gloss_range: root range links safety, security, trust, and belief; the local Form IV selects believing or granting credibility with a fronted falsehood object
words.prose: {{ar:يُؤْمِنُونَ}} ({{tr:yuʾminūna}}) turns the security root into an act of trusting or granting credibility, completed by the fronted falsehood phrase. The result is paradoxical: the root that named real sanctuary security now names trust directed to the void. As the first of two matched imperfect accusation verbs, it pairs with the denial verb; accepted second-person readings would make the same paired charge a direct address. The charge also reprises the 29:52 triad, but shifts the denial object from God directly to God’s blessing.

topics.headline: belief verb is completed by falsehood object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the moral failure lies in granting credibility to the wrong object.
topics.reason: The verb is governed by a fronted bi-complement selecting the object of belief.

topics.headline: same root shifts from safety to false trust
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the irony of the security root being used for misplaced trust after real security was shown.
topics.reason: The local root repetition from the secure participle to the belief verb licenses the reversal.

topics.headline: belief and denial form a matched antithesis
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees belief-in-falsehood and denial-of-blessing as one balanced moral inversion.
topics.reason: The adjacent imperfect verbs form the closing paired accusation.

topics.headline: accepted person shift makes accusation direct
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the variant can turn the closing pair into direct confrontation while preserving the same objects and architecture.
topics.reason: The second-person variant is valid contrastive evidence but does not replace the base third-person surface.

topics.headline: belief in falsehood reprises 29:52 with a changed denial object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader recognizes the 29:52 triad returning, now sharpened from denial of God to denial of God’s blessing.
topics.reason: The concrete same-surah parallel is locally coherent and preserves the changed object.

words.gloss_range: coordinating connector pairing the two accusation clauses
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) at this point coordinates the two charges: believing in falsehood and denying God’s blessing. Unlike the earlier circumstantial {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}), this one makes the two prepositional frames mutually interpretive, so misplaced belief is read as the counterpart of ingratitude.

topics.headline: coordination binds belief and denial as one compound charge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the two final faults as two faces of one inversion, not separate accusations.
topics.reason: The connector coordinates the second accusatory clause with the first.

topics.headline: particle shifts from circumstance to coordination
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ayah’s move from evidence-scene contrast to moral pairing.
topics.reason: The two waw instances have distinct local discourse functions.

words.gloss_range: object-marking preposition attaching denial to the divine blessing
words.prose: {{ar:بِ}} ({{tr:bi}}) with the denial verb marks what is denied or treated with ingratitude, not a means by which they deny. Because the blessing phrase is fronted, the blessing is placed before the denial verb and set in exact parallel with the falsehood phrase.

topics.headline: preposition selects the object of ingratitude
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the final denial targets a specific blessing, not belief in the abstract.
topics.reason: The preposition governs the blessing phrase as complement of the denial verb.

topics.headline: fronted complement makes the blessing visible first
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears God’s blessing before hearing the act of denial, sharpening the charge.
topics.reason: The proclitic and fronted phrase focus the object before the verb.

topics.headline: same preposition frames opposite objects
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees falsehood and blessing as matched alternatives in the moral inversion.
topics.reason: The repeated fronted bi-phrase order foregrounds the two objects as the real contrast.

words.gloss_range: singular construct blessing identified as God’s sanctuary provision
words.root_gloss_range: root range includes ease, favor, blessing, provision, comfort, pastoral abundance, and bliss; the local construct selects a bestowed divine benefit, concretely the secure sanctuary
words.prose: {{ar:نِعْمَةِ}} ({{tr:niʿmati}}) is singular and construct-bound to the divine name, so the blessing is definite through its divine source rather than a vague piece of good fortune. Context points it back to the secure sanctuary: the protected precinct is the visible favor being covered over. The word also joins a recurring denial-of-blessing formula (16:72), while in this ayah the formula is specialized by the sanctuary proof and opposed to standalone falsehood. Within the surah, the same favor field contrasts with the favorable reward language of 29:58.

topics.headline: construct grammar makes blessing source-bound
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the blessing is defined by God as giver, not by anonymous good fortune.
topics.reason: The construct relation and subjective genitive reading are locally licensed.

topics.headline: context identifies the blessing as secure sanctuary provision
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the final blessing as the same secure sanctuary introduced in the proof clause.
topics.reason: The preceding sanctuary-security phrase provides the concrete referent for the denied blessing.

topics.headline: broad ease and favor field narrows to bestowed provision
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the blessing as sustaining favor, while livestock, affirmation, and bliss branches remain background rather than selected senses.
topics.reason: The root field supports abundance and favor but local syntax selects divine blessing.

topics.headline: denied blessing links formulas and same-surah contrast
topics.reader_payoff: The reader recognizes denial of blessing as a recurring charge (16:72) and a same-surah contrast with favorable reward (29:58).
topics.reason: Concrete references preserve formulaic and same-surah payoffs without controlling the local referent.

topics.headline: relational blessing opposes standalone falsehood
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that falsehood stands alone while blessing is relationally tied to God.
topics.reason: The formal contrast between definite abstract and divine construct is locally visible.

topics.headline: prior enjoyment becomes named divine benefit
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the prior boundary’s enjoyment language reframed as dependence on a specific divine gift (29:66).
topics.reason: The boundary rows coherently connect the unnamed prior benefit with this named blessing.

words.gloss_range: genitive divine proper name anchoring the blessing’s source
words.root_gloss_range: proper divine name with lexical discussions around worship, devotion, and awe; locally it functions as the definite genitive source of the blessing
words.prose: {{ar:ٱللَّهِ}} ({{tr:Allāhi}}) is the genitive second member of the blessing construct, making the secure sanctuary God’s provision rather than their achievement or a product of falsehood. The proper name gives the phrase definiteness and direct source, so the closing charge is not just denial but denial of a blessing explicitly attributed to God. Broader worship and awe associations remain secondary coloring around that local genitive role.

topics.headline: proper name anchors blessing as God’s provision
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that sanctuary safety is sourced in God, not in the group or in falsehood.
topics.reason: The noun is genitive as the construct complement of blessing.

topics.headline: proper-name definiteness identifies the blessing
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the blessing made definite through the singular divine proper name.
topics.reason: The proper name, not a generic deity term, transfers definiteness through the construct.

topics.headline: divine name makes benefactor explicit
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the absurdity of denying a benefit whose giver is named inside the object phrase.
topics.reason: The proper name inside the final fronted object phrase grounds the benefactor relation.

topics.headline: root dispute colors preference for falsehood over God’s blessing
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices worship and trust pressure around the divine name, while the local grammar remains a genitive source relation.
topics.reason: Root-dispute and co-occurrence evidence color the contrast but do not change the construct parse.

topics.headline: same-surah divine-source theme returns in the closing object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the sanctuary proof folded into the surah’s broader divine-source and provision thread.
topics.reason: The same-surah recurrence is coherent and anchored in the local blessing phrase.

words.gloss_range: Form I imperfect denial as ongoing ingratitude toward the blessing
words.root_gloss_range: root range moves from covering to denial, ingratitude, and disbelief; the local bi-plus-blessing frame narrows the active sense to covering over a received benefit while theological denial remains in the background
words.prose: {{ar:يَكْفُرُونَ}} ({{tr:yakfurūna}}) closes the ayah with ongoing denial of God’s blessing. Because the verb is completed by the fronted blessing phrase, the active sense is ingratitude or covering over a received benefit, not generic disbelief alone. It stands as the second matched imperfect verb after the belief verb, and the shared plural ending keeps the paired charges rhythmically balanced on the same accused group. The verb also turns the prior projected denial from 29:66 into a present accusation, while the 29:52 triad returns with God’s blessing as the specified denied object.

topics.headline: bi-plus-blessing selects ingratitude toward a benefit
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the final verb targets a concrete received blessing, not disbelief in abstraction.
topics.reason: The governed blessing object narrows the root toward denial of favor.

topics.headline: root image makes denial a covering over of benefit
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees ingratitude as burying or covering the visible sanctuary gift.
topics.reason: The root image survives locally because the object is a received blessing.

topics.headline: final verb mirrors and opposes belief verb
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the closing pair as trust granted to falsehood and denial given to blessing.
topics.reason: The adjacent imperfect verbs and root pair create the moral antithesis.

topics.headline: accepted second-person variant makes the pair confrontational
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the variant can intensify the charge as direct address while preserving the same denial object.
topics.reason: The variant is valid contrastive evidence but does not replace the base third-person surface.

topics.headline: final position turns prior projected denial into present accusation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the ayah land on active ongoing ingratitude, explaining the prior warning (29:66).
topics.reason: The final imperfect reprises and actualizes the prior boundary’s denial language.

topics.headline: denial root reprises earlier falsehood-belief contrast with specified object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader recognizes the earlier triad from 29:52 and the boundary from 29:66, now specified as denial of God’s blessing.
topics.reason: Concrete same-surah echoes add provenance while preserving the local object of denial.

topics.headline: matched endings and subject continuity close the couplet
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the two charges as a balanced couplet landing on the same accused group.
topics.reason: The shared ending and third-person plural subject support rhythmic and referential continuity.

baseline_models.mechanism: The ayah draws a bounded topology: an inviolable, heart-settling center persists while rapid seizure operates in the immediately surrounding ring. The contrast makes the enclave's continued security an observable event, not generic background comfort.

activation_trace.role: The spatial sanctuary supplies an inviolable center and makes security topological.
Heart-settling safety characterizes the center and links its condition to the later belief verb.
Rapid snatching makes the surrounding zone one of unstable removal.
The encircling direction places predation immediately around, rather than remotely from, the protected center.

changed_reading.before: The ayah merely notes that one locality is safe while neighboring people face violence.
changed_reading.after: It stages security as a bounded center exposed against a ring of seizure, making the enclave's persistence itself the visible datum.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: `ءَامِنًا` and `يُؤْمِنُونَ` share ء م ن, while the latter takes `ٱلْبَٰطِلِ`.
baseline_models.mechanism: The same root moves from an experienced condition of safety to a heart's settled credence. They inhabit security made by God yet settle trust in what lacks truth and stability, so false belief becomes parasitic on the safety it miscredits.

activation_trace.role: Making something assume a condition marks the secure state as effected rather than self-originating.
Security and trust supply the experienced condition from which the repeated root pivots.
Heart-settled assent supplies the second pole: the recipients invest credence in an object.
Loss of truth and stability makes that trusted object unable to ground the security experienced.

changed_reading.before: The ayah contrasts physical safety with an unrelated doctrinal error.
changed_reading.after: It turns the same امن root from granted security into misplaced heart-settlement: they experience a God-made secure condition yet entrust themselves to what cannot remain.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: `أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْا أَنَّا جَعَلْنَا ... وَبِنِعْمَةِ ٱللَّهِ يَكْفُرُونَ`
baseline_models.mechanism: Perception, effected condition, gift, and covering form a causal sequence. The safe precinct is a benefit that should disclose its giver; kufr names both ingratitude and the act of putting a cover over what the visible condition reveals.

changed_reading.before: Kufr is only a refusal to say thanks for a benefit.
changed_reading.after: Kufr is a perceptual act: it covers the visible gift and its maker even while the protected condition remains in view.

context_deltas.mechanism: The opening separates saying 'we believe' from the testing that discloses truthfulness. Against that sequence, the focus ayah's secure condition cannot certify the later act of believing: granted amn and tested iman share a root but are not interchangeable achievements.

activation_trace.role: The shared root anchors the distinction in the focus ayah's physical security and fiduciary settlement.

structural_cues: 29:2 places the spoken belief claim before a negated exemption from testing; 29:3 makes testing disclose the truthful and the liars.
29:67 places the secure adjective and false belief under one repeated root.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies repeated امن, then an assay-to-truth sequence; I infer that material safety is evidence and gift but not a certificate of authentic faith. A live alternative is that the opening test addresses a different group without qualifying the sanctuary scene.

changed_reading.before: Experienced security should itself amount to or guarantee correct belief.
changed_reading.after: Security is a gift and sign, not a test-passing certificate; ease can coexist with a heart settled in falsehood.

context_deltas.mechanism: The earlier provisioning sequence names fabricated objects, denies them power of disposal over provision, redirects the search for provision to God, and ends in gratitude. This turns the focus pairing of falsehood and covered blessing into one attribution error: a powerless construct receives the credit due to the actual giver.

activation_trace.role: What lacks truth and stability anchors the counterfeit account in the focus ayah.

A lie turned away from truth gives the alternative objects their fabricated status.

Apportioned giving supplies the concrete good whose source must be sought and credited.
Recognizing a benefit and praising its giver supplies the response opposite to focus-ayah kufr.

structural_cues: 29:17 moves in one ayah from fabricated objects, through their lack of control over provision, to seeking provision from God and thanking Him.
29:67 likewise coordinates belief in falsehood with covering God's benefit.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a powerless-fabrication to provision to gratitude sequence; I infer that believing falsehood includes assigning provider-status to what cannot provide. A live alternative keeps الباطل broader than provisioning even though provision is the clearest contextual instance.

changed_reading.before: Falsehood is an abstract wrong belief and ingratitude is an additional fault.
changed_reading.after: Falsehood functions as a counterfeit provisioning account: credit goes to powerless constructs, so God's actually received provision is simultaneously covered.

context_deltas.mechanism: The spider-house comparison gives false reliance an architecture. Substitute protectors generate a self-made dwelling that looks like refuge but has minimal structural strength; placed beside the focus sanctuary, الباطل becomes a rival shelter-system rather than only a false proposition.

activation_trace.role: The spatial sanctuary supplies the real protected dwelling against which the contextual house is read.

Dwelling and refuge give the substitute alliance a built shelter-image.

structural_cues: 29:41 explicitly compares taking other protectors to a spider taking a house and calls that house the weakest of houses.
29:67 contrasts a genuinely secure precinct with belief in what lacks stability.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies substitute protectors, a self-made weak house, and a secure sanctuary; I infer that the focus falsehood includes rival architectures of protection. A live alternative reads the spider image as dependency in general rather than specifically as a counter-sanctuary.

changed_reading.before: They trust an unspecified false proposition despite real safety.
changed_reading.after: They exchange a divinely maintained sanctuary for a self-spun protective network whose shelter is structurally weakest.

context_deltas.mechanism: An earlier ayah uses the exact sequence 'believe in falsehood / disbelieve in God' and names the result as loss. The focus reprises the first half but changes the second object from God to God's benefit, translating theological denial into the concrete reception and miscrediting of security.

activation_trace.role: The focus object is a bestowed good condition, making the later formula experiential.
Ingratitude and covering of benefit specify how denial appears within security.
Heart-settled assent begins the repeated formula.

Denial that blocks the truth takes God directly as its earlier object.
General diminishment names the outcome of that false-belief and denial pair.

structural_cues: 29:52 coordinates believing in falsehood, disbelieving in God, and being the losers.
29:67 repeats believing in falsehood but replaces direct denial of God with covering God's benefit.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies an exact formula with a changed object; I infer that the later wording diagnoses God-denial at the level of lived receipt and attribution. A live alternative treats the object shift as rhetorical variation rather than a move from doctrine to experience.

changed_reading.before: The ending only repeats generic unbelief language.
changed_reading.after: The repeated formula descends from denying God to covering God's concrete benefit: loss becomes diagnosable in how security is received and credited.

context_deltas.mechanism: The immediately preceding movement runs from peril at sea, through exclusive devotion, to rescue onto dry land, renewed association, covering what was given, and enjoyment. The focus sanctuary is the stabilized land-side version of that sequence: safety is not merely ignored after rescue but becomes the condition in which urgent source-recognition relaxes.

Covering a received benefit explicitly names the post-rescue response.
Enjoyed utility supplies the mode in which the covered benefit continues to be consumed.

structural_cues: 29:65-66 immediately precede the focus and order the events as peril, exclusive invocation, rescue, land, association, benefit-covering, and enjoyment.
29:67 then points to an enduring secure place amid surrounding seizure.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies immediate chronology; I infer a psychological arrow in which regained safety affords the relaxation of crisis-sincerity into rival attribution. A live alternative is temporal succession without safety itself enabling the lapse.

changed_reading.before: They are ungrateful even though they are safe.
changed_reading.after: Safety is the post-rescue condition in which emergency sincerity relaxes into rival attribution and consumption; the gift becomes the occasion of forgetting its giver.

context_deltas.mechanism: The migration-facing sequence widens God's earth, joins patience to reliance, and says creatures need not carry their own allotted provision. This prevents the focus sanctuary from becoming a fetishized coordinate: its security is one visible instance of a provider-relation that can be trusted beyond the enclave.

structural_cues: 29:56 declares God's earth wide and redirects worship to Him.
29:59-60 join patience and reliance to creatures that do not carry their own provision because God provides.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies widened land, endurance, reliance, and provision not self-carried; I infer that the sanctuary manifests a portable provider-relation rather than exhausting security in one locality. A live alternative limits the sequence to reassurance for migrants while preserving the sanctuary as a unique local sign.

changed_reading.before: Security is tied to remaining within one inviolable location.
changed_reading.after: The sanctuary is one visible instance of a portable provider-relation: land can widen, provision need not be carried, and trust can persist beyond the enclave.

context_deltas.mechanism: The nearby interrogations elicit the correct verbal answer that God creates and revives, yet the speakers are described as turned away and not reasoning. Thus 'have they not seen?' does not primarily request missing information; it indicts failure to let an acknowledged cause govern trust, gratitude, and action.

activation_trace.role: Eye or insight anchors the focus demand that available evidence become recognition.

Covering benefit names the practical failure despite available causal knowledge.
Questioning elicits an explicit attribution of cosmic making.

Being turned from a proper direction supplies the break between confession and allegiance.
Rain-revived earth supplies a visible provisioning analogue to the secure sanctuary.
The intellect that restrains ignorance supplies the missing operation that should bind cause to response.

structural_cues: 29:61 says their answer to who created and subjected the heavenly bodies will be God, then asks how they are turned away.
29:63 repeats their answer over rain and revived earth, then says most do not reason.
29:67 again uses a rhetorical perception question before false belief and ingratitude.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies correct answers followed by turning and non-reasoning; I infer that the focus defect lies in causal and fiduciary integration, not simple ignorance. A live alternative is that the speakers' answers are merely compelled conventions with no genuine recognition.

changed_reading.before: They fail to notice who made the sanctuary.
changed_reading.after: They may already verbalize the correct maker; the failure is inferential and fiduciary, refusing to bind acknowledged causation to trust and gratitude.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it projects later punishment geometry back onto a present sanctuary scene. It remains anchored in the focus contrast between `حَوْلِهِمْ`, security, and kufr, while 29:54-55 supplies enclosing, overlying, and underfoot directions. Render it as a topological echo and possible reversal, not as a claim that the sanctuary itself becomes the enclosing punishment.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The protected center has seizure `مِنْ حَوْلِهِمْ`, while the verse ends in kufr.

activation_trace.role: The surrounding direction supplies a ring of danger outside the current protected center.

Enclosure by overpowering destruction turns an external ring into the unbeliever's containing condition.

The upper direction specifies one face of total enclosure.
The under-direction closes the topology beneath the person.

changed_reading.before: Danger remains outside the secure center.
changed_reading.after: The topology can reverse: continued covering turns the person from a protected center with danger around it into the one encircled and overlaid by consequence.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is branch-distant because it activates the تعطّل واللهو range of بطل rather than treating that range as the direct gloss of `ٱلْبَٰطِلِ`. It remains anchored in the focus root and in 29:64's immediately preceding distraction/play pair. Render it as an exploratory material analogy: a transient play-world is trusted as infrastructure, not as a lexical replacement for falsehood.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: `أَفَبِٱلْبَٰطِلِ يُؤْمِنُونَ` places settled credence in بطل.

activation_trace.role: Idleness, non-benefit, and following diversion supply an exploratory lived texture for the false object of trust.
Settled assent turns that transient texture into something treated as dependable.
Distraction by one thing from another supplies the mechanism that hides the lasting source of safety.
Action without a sound end supplies the unstable world that is nevertheless inhabited as shelter.

changed_reading.before: Falsehood is simply a proposition without truth.
changed_reading.after: Falsehood can be a transient play-world treated as stable infrastructure: distraction is inhabited as though it were a sanctuary.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it activates the branch image of `مَعْقِل` as refuge from the context root عقل and maps it onto the focus sanctuary. It remains valid as an anchored cross-domain analogy between an outer protected precinct and the absent reasoning named in 29:63. Render it as wordplay-assisted mechanism, not as an etymological claim that عقل in 29:63 literally means fortress.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: An outer `حَرَمًا ءَامِنًا` is visible, yet its evidence does not secure the observers' response.

activation_trace.role: The protected spatial precinct supplies the external refuge.
Reflection and considered judgment supply the internal uptake the rhetorical question demands.
The branch image of a refuge or fortress supplies an exploratory internal counterpart to the sanctuary.
Reason as a restraint on ignorance states the actual contextual deficit that makes the fortress analogy functional.

changed_reading.before: Possession of an outer sanctuary should make its inhabitants secure in judgment.
changed_reading.after: An outer refuge cannot substitute for the inner holding-function of reason; the sign is physically entered but not inferentially inhabited.

strongest_changes: The shared امن root now distinguishes granted safety from the trust that recipients misplace in what cannot remain.
The spider house turns falsehood into a rival shelter-system, while the rescue-to-land sequence shows how regained safety can become the condition of forgetting.
The repeated 29:52 formula moves from denying God to covering God's concrete benefit, locating theological loss inside everyday receipt and attribution.
The creation and rain interrogations show that correct verbal attribution can coexist with failure to bind cause to trust and gratitude.
summary.what_was_special: Whole-surah recurrence changed the focus from a static contrast between a safe place and outside violence into a mechanism of shelter, source-attribution, and post-rescue memory. The sanctuary is simultaneously visible evidence, received provision, a counter-image to self-spun refuge, and a test of whether safety settles the heart in its giver or in a substitute.
remaining_uncertainties: The adjacent rescue sequence supports, but does not force, the causal claim that regained safety enables relapse rather than merely preceding it.
The widened-earth and provision sequence may portablely generalize the sanctuary's provider-relation, but the local precinct remains a distinctive sign.
The enclosure reversal, play-world, and inner-fortress readings should remain qualified echoes rather than primary lexical readings.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **Protected bounds made visible by surrounding seizure.** ح ر م B003 is an inviolable precinct with protected bounds, and B006 is inviolable claim, pact, and respect. Safety inside is contrasted with people being snatched from around them, making the boundary empirically legible. I infer that the enclave's security is a granted relation, not self-generated terrain; belief in falsehood and covering the favor read as a reversal of the sanctuary's visible causal lesson.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 29:68 answers the protected precinct with Hell as مثوى. The contrast turns place into moral relation: one bounded space is a recognized gift, the other an assigned lodging for covering that gift.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Security is a bounded, visible state inside a surrounding field of seizure.** Lexical evidence: `يَرَوْا`, root `ر ء ي`, `B001` (seeing by eye or insight); `جَعَلْنَا`, root `ج ع ل`, `B002` (turning something into a state); `حَرَمًا`, root `ح ر م`, `B003` (inviolable precinct and protected bounds); `ءَامِنًا`, root `ء م ن`, `B001` (settled security); `يُتَخَطَّف`, root `خ ط ف`, `B001` (swift snatching); and `حَوْلِهِم`, root `ح و ل`, `B004` (space around a thing). Structural cue: protected center and snatching circumference are placed in one visual field. Assigned role: making establishes the state, sacred bounds delimit it, and surrounding seizure makes the protection contrastively visible. Abductive move: I infer that the spatial contrast functions as evidence of bestowed security rather than ordinary regional uniformity. Reading change: sanctuary is a demonstrable protected exception, not an abstract label.

2. **The same security-root exposes trust placed against lived security.** Lexical evidence: `ءَامِنًا / يُؤْمِنُون`, root `ء م ن`, respectively `B001` (security) and `B002` (trusting assent); `ٱلْبَاطِل`, root `ب ط ل`, `B001` (voidness); `نِعْمَة`, root `ن ع م`, `B001` (bestowed favor); and `يَكْفُرُون`, root `ك ف ر`, `B004` (covering over a favor). Structural cue: they inhabit one root as objective safety but attach the same root's trust branch to voidness, then cover the actual favor. Assigned role: lived security supplies evidence; trust chooses an object; covering severs the evidence-object relation. Abductive move: the lexical recurrence supplies the contradiction, and I infer a failure to let experienced protection govern allegiance. Reading change: the ayah presents unbelief as trust placed opposite to the source of one's own safety.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: - **Later correction (`29:68-69`):** Denial of arriving firm truth exposes the endpoint of trusting voidness, while guided plural ways offer the alternative. Sanctuary security is therefore a visible directional sign: it can be misread into false trust or followed toward the source's ways.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: Security is produced by a bounded interior and is exposed by the speed with which predatory taking operates outside it.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: Sacred security becomes perimeter law, buffer zone, obstacle, hooked extraction, and the difference between trusted stillness and high-speed capture.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Bounded Interior, Buffer, and Protected Right
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: A protected center is established, surrounded by a legally meaningful buffer, and held apart from external access.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: prohibition that blocks violation `quranic:root_000313:B001/m01`; sacred precinct and spatial buffer `quranic:root_000313:B003/m01`; protected right and inviolable bond `quranic:root_000313:B006/m01`; inward security and trust `quranic:root_000054:B001/m01`; surrounding direction `quranic:root_000373:B004/m01`; barrier separating two sides `quranic:root_000373:B005/m01`; placing something into a protected state `quranic:root_000248:B002/m01`
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: The sanctuary is not merely a point but a center-plus-buffer system. Prohibition, right, surrounding zone, and separating barrier make security spatially and normatively produced.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: Security is produced by a bounded interior and is exposed by the speed with which predatory taking operates outside it.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: Sacred security becomes perimeter law, buffer zone, obstacle, hooked extraction, and the difference between trusted stillness and high-speed capture.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Hooked Snatching Beyond the Boundary
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: Outside the protected interior, a fast taker uses sudden grip or hook to extract exposed persons before stable response is possible.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: rapid seizure and stripping `quranic:root_000423:B001/m01`; hooked iron or claw `quranic:root_000423:B002/m01`; predatory or human snatcher `quranic:root_000423:B003/m01`; neck-drawn speed in flight `quranic:root_000423:B004/m01`; exposed surrounding zone `quranic:root_000373:B004/m01`; direct visual apprehension `quranic:root_000531:B001/m01`; land as exposed supporting field `quranic:root_000025:B001/m01`
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: The outside is defined by extraction speed: grip, hook, predator, and accelerated withdrawal leave little time for collective defense. The verse's contrast thus measures sanctuary by the predatory mechanics it suspends.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_channel: P5 (29:57-69) Fabricated Appearance Against Fitted Truth
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: Falsehood is made by cutting, coating, or turning material away from its proper fit; truth is what remains fixed and correctly joined.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: Lying becomes leatherwork, destructive cutting, counterfeit plating, false-colored cloth, and a misaligned joint.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Turning Away From the Proper Fit
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: A claim is rotated away from its correct orientation, while truth is tested by whether assertion, evidence, and fitting place coincide.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: turning a thing from its proper direction `quranic:root_000041:B001/m01`; weakened judgment after diversion `quranic:root_000041:B006/m01`; truth fixed to reality `quranic:root_000347:B001/m01`; proof that manifests truth `quranic:root_000347:B005/m01`; part fitting its proper joint or receptacle `quranic:root_000347:B011/m01`; falsehood without stability `quranic:root_000127:B001/m01`; false assertion `quranic:root_000127:B003/m01`; contradiction of truth in speech or act `quranic:root_001290:B001/m01`
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Falsehood is directional failure: statement and evidence are turned away from the place where they should meet. Truth is the opposite operation, a stable match like a part seated in its proper joint.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_channel: P5 (29:57-69) Worldly Life as Game and Distraction
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: Immediate play diverts attention from a deferred reality and consumes or risks what should sustain purposeful life.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: Diversion becomes aimless performance, wind-erased tracks, wager, mill-feed, and the exchange of a deferred outcome for an immediate stake.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Aimless Performance and Diverted Attention
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: An activity expends motion without a sound end while another attraction turns attention away from the lasting object.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: play lacking a valid aim `quranic:root_001358:B001/m01`; wind playing through and erasing a place `quranic:root_001358:B005/m01`; occupation that turns one away from another object `quranic:root_001382:B001/m01`; amusement and enjoyed diversion `quranic:root_001382:B002/m01`; the near and lower life `quranic:root_000493:B002/m01`; what comes after the first `quranic:root_000019:B001/m01`; useless inactivity `quranic:root_000127:B005/m01`
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Worldly play is not condemned because it moves, but because its motion has no stable end and is easily erased like tracks under wind. Distraction compounds the loss by turning attention from the later reality that gives action an enduring object.
